selected_mechanism.name: Rural Health Transformation Program pass-through: CMS allotment to DOH Commissioner's discretionary subaward decision

news_trigger.quote: The Alaska Department of Health is preparing to accept applications for the second year of a federal program intended to transform rural healthcare, even as the state has yet to finish distributing the first round of funding it received.
news_trigger.what_happened: The Alaska Department of Health is preparing to accept applications for the second year of a federal program intended to transform rural healthcare, even as the state has yet to finish distributing the first round of funding it received.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A $50B federal statutory fund (SSA 2105(h)) that CMS allots to states against a plan required to 'prioritize data and technology driven solutions', which in Alaska ($272,174,856 in Year 1) funnels through a single discretionary decision point, the DOH Commissioner, with the Alaska Community Foundation administering subawards on the Commissioner's behalf.

layers.name: Statutory appropriation and plan mandate
layers.what_it_does: Appropriates $10B per year FY2026-FY2030; requires state rural health transformation plans that 'prioritize the use of new and emerging technologies' and 'prioritize data and technology driven solutions'.
layers.controlling_actor: Congress (fixed statute, 42 U.S.C. 1397ee(h)); not a live decision layer

layers.name: Federal allotment and clawback
layers.what_it_does: Approves or denies state applications and sets each approved state's allotment annually; half allocated on rural-population and facility factors; the Administrator 'may withhold payments to, or reduce payments to, or recover previous payments from, the State... as the Administrator deems appropriate.'
layers.controlling_actor: Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (office)

layers.name: State lead agency and final award authority
layers.what_it_does: Receives Alaska's Year 1 award of $272,174,856 and makes all funding decisions: 'Under Alaska law and consistent with our CMS approved RHTP application, the DOH Commissioner retains final decision-making authority on all funding decisions.'
layers.controlling_actor: Commissioner, Alaska Department of Health (incumbent Heidi Hedberg), advised by the RHTP Advisory Council (advisory only)

layers.name: Subaward administration and intake
layers.what_it_does: Runs the LOI/application portal and manages the subaward process: 'DOH has contracted with ACF to support implementation of RHTP in Alaska by managing the subaward process on behalf of DOH.'
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska Community Foundation, contracted subaward manager for DOH

layers.name: Year 2 state-directed targeting
layers.what_it_does: Shifts Year 2 from open calls toward 'state-directed targeted innovation funding opportunities focused on complex or statewide priority areas'; new LOI/application period 'as early as fall 2026'. ADN reports the three Year 2 focus areas: pay-for-value reimbursement, care coordination, and emergency medical services.
layers.controlling_actor: DOH Commissioner (sets criteria and final awards); public comment on criteria is advisory

illustrative_examples.what: Foundation Health Partners $16M award for data and technology to better focus on prevention (example only, not a layer)
Rep. Genevieve Mina: federal design is 'almost directing us to AI'

chokepoint.layer: State lead agency and final award authority
chokepoint.actor: Commissioner, Alaska Department of Health (office; current incumbent Heidi Hedberg)
chokepoint.binary_decision: Fund or do not fund each RHTP subaward, and set the Year 2 state-directed criteria; the program is discretionary and the Advisory Council only advises. Secondary upstream binary: CMS Administrator withhold/reduce/recover.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: The federal statute tilts toward technology ('prioritize data and technology driven solutions'), but the Alaska layer routes that tilt through one discretionary office. Year 1 went out as stabilization in weekly batches, and Year 2 narrows discretion further into state-directed calls in three named areas, none labelled technology. For Alaska AI and health-IT vendors the money is real but not addressed to them; it arrives via provider subrecipients whose projects fit the Commissioner's categories, with the tech mandate sitting upstream. The CMS Administrator's withhold/recoup power pressures against slow disbursement.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Health-tech and AI vendors should comment on the Year 2 criteria by the Oct. 9 deadline reported by ADN and line up a provider partner (hospital, tribal health organization, or EMS agency) whose project fits pay-for-value, care coordination, or EMS before state-directed calls open, rather than planning a standalone vendor application.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Health IT / AI: Alaska rural providers and their technology vendors must shape Year 2 proposals around the Commissioner's three state-directed focus areas, from now through the October 2026 criteria comment window and the end-of-October release of remaining Year 1 funds; Year 1 funds must be fully spent by 2027-09-30.
